subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw satisfy Codex external-auth refresh callbacks from a still-usable cached OpenAI OAuth token, or preserve forced refresh and wait for upstream Codex timeout configurability?
rationale: The code fix is not just a timeout constant: it changes auth freshness, external runtime behavior, and operator recovery semantics across OpenClaw and Codex, so maintainers need to choose the product/security contract before a repair PR.

options.title: Use cached-valid token fast path
options.body: Recommended: return a still-usable cached OAuth access token for Codex refresh callbacks, reserve slow refresh for expired credentials, and surface targeted re-auth/degraded health when refresh is required but cannot complete in time.

options.title: Wait for upstream configurability
options.body: Keep forced refresh semantics and track the upstream Codex timeout request, accepting that shipped OpenClaw runtimes can still hit the 10-second callback deadline until the dependency changes.

options.title: Fold into broader auth hardening
options.body: Defer this issue to the broader runtime-auth deadline and fallback policy work, but keep this issue open as the valid-refresh 10-second callback acceptance criterion.

recommendation.title: Use cached-valid token fast path
recommendation.body: Recommended: return a still-usable cached OAuth access token for Codex refresh callbacks, reserve slow refresh for expired credentials, and surface targeted re-auth/degraded health when refresh is required but cannot complete in time.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent review and code history put steipete closest to the Codex app-server and OAuth fallback contract choice.
